questions.question: Name three daily uses and two other uses of water, and say which uses the most water in South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Daily uses: drinking, cooking, washing ourselves, washing clothes and dishes, cleaning and flushing toilets. Other uses: farming, factories, mines, making electricity, gardens and recreation. Farming uses the most water in South Africa.

questions.question: Describe the water cycle and name three ways people get their water.
questions.expected_answer: The sun heats water and it evaporates as vapour, leaving salt behind; the vapour cools and condenses into clouds; precipitation falls as rain, hail or snow; and water is collected in rivers, lakes and underground before flowing back to the sea. People get water from rivers, streams and springs; from wells and boreholes; from water trucks; and from taps, after it is cleaned at a treatment works.

questions.question: Give three examples of how communication has changed over time, and one way it has stayed the same.
questions.expected_answer: Letters carried by runners, coaches and ships changed to the telegraph, which sent Morse code along wires, and the telephone, which carried voices. Radio and television reached millions at once. Cell phones, cameras, computers and the internet now send messages, photos and videos around the world in seconds. People still talk face to face, tell stories and write letters.
